first_impression.reaction: I typed 'santorini wedding' on the train. The first paragraph gives me the whole plan in one sentence: legal or symbolic, season, setting, guests, travel, documents, rules, weekend. No pop-up, no fluff, and the steps are numbered so I can jump. I'd read the takeaways, go to the season step, look at the capacity table, glance at the checklist and the FAQ. Then bookmark. It's long for a phone, but the headings make that OK.

journey.quote: Planning a Santorini wedding comes down to a short run of decisions: legal or symbolic, then the season, the setting, the guest list, how everyone arrives, the documents, the house rules and the weekend around the day.
journey.reaction: That's the answer in the first 60 words. I know what the page is and whether I need it.

journey.quote: Choose your season from official weather data and current travel advice, and set the ceremony time around the summer heat and the north wind.
journey.reaction: OK, but which season? This is the takeaway I actually wanted and it tells me how to choose instead of what to choose. I have to scroll to the table.

journey.quote: Put every house rule in writing before you sign, including music times, exclusive use, ceremony times and the plan if the weather turns.
journey.reaction: Practical. Didn't think about music cut-off times at all.

journey.section: Why couples choose Santorini for their wedding
journey.quote: It is not one island but a cluster: Thera, Thirasia, Aspronisi, Palea Kameni and Nea Kameni.
journey.reaction: Interesting trivia, but I've already picked Santorini. Scrolling past to Step 1.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: Dated, which I like. But it's all about Australia and I'm not Australian, so I skip to the next heading. Clearly labelled, so no harm done.

journey.quote: Grace Hotel in Imerovigli offers a unity ceremony in which the two of you combine black and white volcanic sand collected from Santorini beaches.
journey.reaction: Oh, that's lovely. I'd screenshot that for my partner.

journey.quote: | Month (Naxos station) | Mean maximum °C | Mean temperature °C | Rain (mm) | Rain days |
journey.reaction: Five columns on a phone is a squeeze, and 'mean maximum' next to 'mean temperature' takes a second to read. At least it tells me straight that it's Naxos, not Santorini.

journey.quote: May and September sit between, with mean maximums of 22.1°C and 25.1°C.
journey.reaction: This is the line I was after. It should be up in the takeaways, not under the table.

journey.quote: Ferry services can be delayed or cancelled in bad weather, mainly because of strong winds.
journey.reaction: Bold lead-ins make this easy to skim. The ferry and wind bit is genuinely useful, I'd have assumed ferries just run.

journey.quote: The 363 Lounge, an open-air champagne terrace, seats 40 or holds 60 standing.
journey.reaction: Real names and real numbers. That's what makes me trust a page.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: AUD again. I'm in Singapore. Is this only for Australians?

journey.quote: On the caldera, space is scarce. Check your guest list against the seated number for each space, not the standing one.
journey.reaction: Didn't know that. The table under it is the bit I'd save, though it's a long table to thumb through.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness.
journey.reaction: Lots of Australian paperwork detail. Not for me, skipped the whole step.

journey.quote: Before you sign with any venue, get written answers to each of these:
journey.reaction: A proper checklist. This is what I'd bookmark and send on.

journey.quote: The cost of a Santorini wedding moves with decisions you make in the steps above.
journey.reaction: 'Just tell me how much it costs.' No number anywhere. The bold headings at least tell me what moves the bill.

journey.quote: The tourist season runs from May to October, and lifeguards work at many Greek beaches from June to September.
journey.reaction: I asked when the wedding season is and the first thing I get is lifeguards. It doesn't actually say which months suit a wedding best.

journey.quote: Very. Most caldera-edge spaces in Oia and Imerovigli seat between 15 and 60, and Grace Hotel's villa terrace seats 15.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, first word. More of this.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Santorini wedding cost? Even a ballpark. There isn't a single number on the page.
Which months does the guide actually recommend for a wedding? It gives the data but never says it plainly.
How far ahead should we book a caldera venue?
Is the Wedded Advisor service for people outside Australia, or only Australians?

turn_offs_found.quote: Choose your season from official weather data and current travel advice, and set the ceremony time around the summer heat and the north wind.
turn_offs_found.why: Takeaways are the only part I'm guaranteed to read, and this one tells me how to pick a season without naming one. The useful line (May and September) is buried under the weather table in Step 2.

turn_offs_found.quote: The tourist season runs from May to October, and lifeguards work at many Greek beaches from June to September.
turn_offs_found.why: I often jump straight to the FAQ. This answer opens with tourist season and lifeguards instead of the months that suit a wedding, so my exact question doesn't get a straight answer.

turn_offs_found.quote: | Month (Naxos station) | Mean maximum °C | Mean temperature °C | Rain (mm) | Rain days |
turn_offs_found.why: Five columns on a phone means squinting or scrolling sideways, and two similar temperature columns make me stop and work out which is which. Minor, the sentences under it explain it.

turn_offs_found.quote: It is not one island but a cluster: Thera, Thirasia, Aspronisi, Palea Kameni and Nea Kameni.
turn_offs_found.why: Minor. A geography section sits between the takeaways and Step 1, so it's one more screen before the useful bit. Not a deal-breaker because the intro already answered me.

would_share_with: My partner: the volcanic sand unity ceremony and the booking checklist
A friend who's looking at Greek islands: the capacity table and the ferry and wind notes

cta_reaction.quote: Once you have a setting in mind, [talk to Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding&utm_content=primary).
cta_reaction.why: I'm only looking, I haven't picked a setting. The links didn't get in my way and there were no pop-ups, so no complaint. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the AUD line leaves me unsure they'd work with someone in Singapore.

top_3_changes: Name the months in the season takeaway, for example that May and September sit between the summer heat and the wetter shoulder months, so the takeaways answer 'when' on their own.
Open the 'When is the wedding season in Santorini?' FAQ with the months that suit a wedding and why, then the tourist season and lifeguard detail.
Make the Step 2 weather table easier on a phone, for example by dropping or merging one temperature column, and put the 'May and September sit between' line directly above it.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Title, deferred business details and deliberately unprinted prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing or not-published explanations

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'santorini wedding' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, skimmed 'Why couples choose', read Steps 1 to 4 selectively, skipped most of the Australian legal and document detail, read the checklist, skimmed costs, then the FAQ.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question and a low objection only.
The title, fees and company specifics (including the AUD and Australian focus) are deferred, so they are noted as reader reactions but kept out of top_3_changes.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots, HTML comments and any [[VERIFY]] markers treated as invisible.
Quotes are given as a reader sees them, with inline HTML fact comments removed; link markup kept where the quoted sentence contains a link.
